Definition: probably from the base of G1097; the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning:--mind, understanding. Compare G5590.
BiblicalUsage: Nous is the mind, not just the intellect, but the whole inner person thinking, feeling, and choosing. Jesus opens the minds of His disciples in Luke 24:45 so they can understand the Scriptures, and Paul warns in Ephesians 4:17 against walking in the vanity of the mind like the Gentiles. The same word cuts both ways in Romans 1:28, where God gives people over to a reprobate mind, and in 1 Corinthians 1:10, where believers are to be joined together in the same mind.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mind is a battlefield and a gift at once: God renews it, and we are responsible for what we set it on. That is why I hold that right thinking is not cold religion, it is the way the heart learns to love what God loves.
